service.description: Record an actual outage of a resource, equipment (assetId: an asset that is not stock) or a facility (facilityId), exactly one (design-maintenance Downtime RecordDowntime, review Y3), or link the one that is open: with the resource locked, its open actual outage in force (no thruDate, not superseded) is answered (linked true) and nothing else is written but the work order's link, so two faults of one resource are one outage; else a new one of kind RukActual from fromDate (now when empty), open, or ended at thruDate (a past outage, a supervisor's or resource administrator's), with the reason (ResourceUnavailabilityReason, its planned or unplanned classification kept), the description, and its source: the production downtime or the maintenance work order and step. A work order named links the outage (MaintenanceWorkOrder.resourceUnavailabilityId). Bookings of the resource over it are kept and answered by id (affectedBookingIds). Nothing here ends an outage: end#ResourceUnavailability restores the resource. Two entry points, checked by data: Manufacturing's, sourceProductionDowntimeId an equipment-fault stop of the asset in an organization the user operates (PRODUCTION_OPERATE or PRODUCTION_SUPERVISE), a stop not corrected and with no outage yet, the outage from its start, open and an equipment fault (SOURCE_INVALID otherwise), as ProductionDowntime.js records it; and Maintenance's, MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE or MAINTENANCE_RESOURCE_EDIT on a resource of the user's maintenance scope, or MAINTENANCE_EXECUTE on the work order (or its step) assigned to the user (workEffortId) that targets it, with a reason (REASON_INVALID). Refuses a kind other than RukActual (KIND_INVALID), no resource or two (RESOURCE_REQUIRED), stock or a missing asset (ASSET_INVALID), a resource or work outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), another permission (PERMISSION_DENIED), a technician without work (WORK_REQUIRED) or on work not theirs (NOT_ASSIGNED), work that is no work order on the resource (WORK_INVALID), a step of other work (STEP_INVALID), a source that is no equipment fault of the asset (SOURCE_INVALID), and a start or end in the future or an end before the start (INTERVAL_INVALID).

parameter.name: workEffortId
parameter.description: The maintenance work order (its root) the outage is recorded from

parameter.name: linked
parameter.description: True when an open outage of the resource was answered

service.description: The actual outages of the user's maintenance scope (a work or resource read: MAINTENANCE_VIEW, _ASSIGNED_VIEW or _RESOURCE_VIEW; PERMISSION_DENIED without), newest first, in force unless includeCorrected, scoped and filtered in the query before paging: one outage, organization, equipment, facility (with those inside it and the equipment there), reason, planned or unplanned (planned Y or N), open or ended (open true or false), source (production or work), a work order (the outages it recorded or linked; it must be readable) and a period (fromDate, thruDate overlapping). Each row carries its resource, interval and elapsed time (open ones to now), reason and classification, production context (the stop's work center, reason and run, and how many stops link it), the work orders recorded with or linked, who recorded and who restored it with the disposition, its corrections, the bookings it affects (a count), the open work orders a restoration leaves open (openWorkList), and canRestore and canCorrect for the user. With resourceUnavailabilityId, history is its correction chain. A holder of every organization with an active one lists that organization's.

A correction of an outage in force, a maintenance supervisor's or resource administrator's (MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE or MAINTENANCE_RESOURCE_EDIT, PERMISSION_DENIED) in the user's scope, with its reason (REASON_REQUIRED): a new row with the corrected start, the end of an ended outage, the reason and the description, which keeps who recorded and who restored it, and the corrected row kept with its values, superseded by the new one (supersession, design §6); the work orders linked to it are linked to the new row. Refuses an outage outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), a planned block (KIND_INVALID: Manufacturing's offline time or a blackout), one already corrected (OUTAGE_CORRECTED), a changed revision (REVISION_CHANGED), an end on an open outage, which restoration gives (OUTAGE_OPEN), a reason that is no downtime reason (REASON_INVALID) and an interval in the future or ending before it starts (INTERVAL_INVALID).

The restoration of a resource, the only end of an actual outage (design §6 RestoreResource, §7.1): a maintenance supervisor's or resource administrator's (MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE or MAINTENANCE_RESOURCE_EDIT, PERMISSION_DENIED) in the user's scope, at thruDate (now when empty, not before the start nor in the future), with the disposition, available for use (MdispAvailable) or usable with restrictions (MdispRestricted), and the readiness evidence (endComments). Maintenance work orders linked to the outage that are still open stay open: the answer lists them (openWorkList, as find# does for the dialog), and restoring while any is open needs the reason (openWorkReason, kept on the row; OPEN_WORK names them without one; the user's call of Nov 12). No work order ends an outage: closing the production downtime that recorded it, completing a work order or cancelling one ends nothing, so two work orders on one resource cannot each end the other's. Refuses an outage outside the scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one corrected (OUTAGE_CORRECTED), a planned block (KIND_INVALID), one ended (OUTAGE_ENDED), a changed revision (REVISION_CHANGED), no disposition (DISPOSITION_REQUIRED) or another one (DISPOSITION_INVALID) and an end out of its interval (INTERVAL_INVALID).

parameter.name: openWorkReason
parameter.description: Required while a linked work order is open

parameter.name: openWorkList
parameter.description: The linked work orders still open (workEffortId, workEffortName, statusText, text), which stay open
